column2: 4 deaths – See the section on this tornado – 57 people were injured.
column3: Five homes were destroyed, including three mobile homes, and dozens of other structures sustained varying degree of damage. Four people were injured. Total economic losses were estimated at over $750,000.
column4: Several trees were downed, and a few outbuildings were damaged.
column5: A metal building had part of its roof ripped off and garage doors blown in. Homes and a church sustained minor roof damage, and a sign was blown over. A trampoline was thrown 30 yards, and trees were snapped and uprooted along the path as well. Total economic losses reached $50,000.
column6: A dozen trees were downed, one of which destroyed an outbuilding.
column7: Several structures in Wetumpka were damaged, including a church. Trees were snapped and uprooted as well.
column8: Fencing, trees, and metal siding were damaged at Emerald Mountain Christian Academy.
column9: Two homes suffered roof damage and several trees were snapped.
column10: Several trees were snapped or uprooted.
column11: A mobile home was severely damaged, injuring two occupants. Minor roof and gutter damage was inflicted to other homes, outbuildings were damaged or destroyed, and groves of trees were snapped or uprooted by this long-track but weak tornado. Damage to trees occurred in Troy, one of which was uprooted and landed on a home, causing structural damage. Near the end of the path, homes sustained minor shingle damage in the northern part of Louisville.
column12: A weak tornado damaged shingles and snapped or uprooted several trees.
column13: Several structures sustained damage to their shingles, and numerous pine trees were downed.
column14: Several roofs and wooden fences were damaged.
column15: Dozens of trees were downed. Several buildings at the Smiths Station School Athletic Complex were destroyed, and others were damaged.
column16: Several homes sustained substantial roof damage, an outdoor shelter was destroyed, and numerous large trees were snapped or uprooted. Intense pressure falls near the tornado caused four to six biscuit cans at a super market to pop open. Total economic losses reached $75,000.
column17: Numerous trees were snapped in a wilderness area. Total economic losses reached $10,000.
column18: Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted, a small shed was destroyed, and a small building was overturned. Total economic losses reached $65,000.
column19: Two metal barns were destroyed, a small silo was ripped out of the ground and thrown over {{convert|300|yd|m|abbr=on}}, and numerous trees were snapped or uprooted. A single-story home and a trailer sustained significant roof, window, and siding damage. Total economic losses reached $100,000.
column20: Hundreds of trees were snapped or uprooted. One home was severely damaged while several others sustained less severe roof damage. Total economic losses reached $300,000.
column21: One home sustained significant roof damage, a second sustained moderate roof damage, and a third had its porch ripped off. Numerous trees and power lines were downed as the tornado entered the western part of Thomaston before dissipating. Total economic losses reached $75,000.
column22: Numerous trees were downed or snapped, causing a car accident. Total economic losses reached $20,000.
column23: A home had a portion of its roof ripped off, numerous trees were snapped or uprooted, and an outbuilding lost wood or metal roof panels. Total economic losses reached $20,000.
column24: Three irrigation systems were overturned, structures sustained minor roof damage, and trees were damaged. Total economic losses reached $30,000.
column25: Several dozen trees were snapped or uprooted, and a residence sustained minor roof damage. Total economic losses reached $15,000.
column26: A rain-wrapped tornado damaged dozens of homes, snapped or uprooted countless trees, and downed brick fences in Warner Robins. One home had much its roof torn off, while others were damaged to a lesser degree. Projectiles were driven through exterior walls and into the ground. A sports complex and a business were damaged, and 15 to 20 mobile homes were severely damaged in a mobile home park. Two large HVAC units were tossed 50 yd (46 m) from the top of a Walmart, where the auto bay doors on the back of the store were blown in, the roof was lifted, and rafters were twisted. Total economic losses reached $295,000.
column27: Approximately 100 trees were downed, and one section of an irrigation system was overturned. Total economic losses reached $50,000.
column28: A fence and numerous trees were downed. The roof was lifted off a small barn, three homes sustained roof damage, and an abandoned fire station was damaged. Total economic losses reached $30,000.
column29: Multiple trees were snapped or uprooted. Total economic losses reached $10,000.
column30: Several softwood trees were snapped or uprooted, damaging some homes. Total economic losses reached $25,000.
column31: A couple dozen trees were uprooted. Total economic losses reached $12,000.
column32: Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted. One residence had a portion of its tin roof peeled off while a second sustained damage to its awning and siding. Total economic losses reached $10,000.
column33: A small outbuilding had its metal roof panels ripped off, a metal building sustained major roof damage, and multiple trees were snapped or uprooted. Total economic losses reached $10,000.
column34: One mobile home was destroyed while another was severely damaged. Trees were damaged. Total economic losses reached $30,000.
column35: Shingles were torn from roofs, a shed was destroyed, and a mobile home was rolled and destroyed. Total economic losses reached $50,000.
column36: Numerous trees were downed, including dozens of pecan trees which were uprooted in an orchard. Total economic losses reached $60,000.
column37: An irrigation system was turned over and several trees were downed.
column38: A residence had its porch blown off, an outbuilding was destroyed, an outbuilding had its metal roofing panels ripped off, and numerous trees were snapped or uprooted. Total economic losses reached $50,000.
column39: The roof of a metal barn and several calf weaning huts were damaged.
column40: The exterior wall of a metal building was shredded, and numerous trees were snapped or uprooted.
column41: A carport attached to a residence was damaged, metal roofing was ripped from four storage buildings, and significant tree damage was observed.
column42: Five chicken coops were heavily damaged, with metal roofing scattered {{convert|500|yd|m|abbr=on}} downwind. A home sustained minor shingle damage, and several trees were downed or uprooted.
column43: A motor vehicle was rolled downhill, the northeast wall of a metal firehouse was ripped off, and metal roofing was torn from several houses and outbuildings. A stop sign was tossed {{convert|50|yd|m|abbr=on}}, numerous trees were snapped or uprooted, and six headstones weighing up 200–400 lbs (90–180 kg) were toppled.
column44: Hundreds of softwood and hardwood trees were snapped or uprooted by this large wedge tornado, with numerous trees landing on homes and causing structural damage. Several structures were heavily damaged or destroyed, most notably a mobile home which was rolled several times and had its floors separated from the undercarriage. The inside occupant was injured. Several chicken houses suffered extensive roof damage.
column45: Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted, three mobile homes were heavily damaged, and a metal farm building collapsed.
column46: Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted, and numerous power lines were downed. One home had its roof ripped off while several others were damaged to a lesser extent, many by falling trees. Mobile homes were also damaged, outbuildings were destroyed, and a vehicle was overturned as well. Total economic losses reached $1,000,000.
column47: Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted, and numerous power lines were downed. A single-wide mobile home had its roof ripped off, and a tree landed on an outbuilding. Total economic losses reached $250,000.
column48: A strong wedge tornado passed near the town of Vivian, snapping and uprooting numerous trees and downing many power lines. Several vehicles were pushed, a party barge boat was moved {{convert|200|yd|m|abbr=on}} into a grove of trees, and a travel trailer was flipped. The roof was ripped off a house, and a mobile home was shifted off its foundation. A woman was taking shelter in a bathtub inside the house that had its torn off. The tornado carried her through the air while she was in the tub and then deposited her in a wooded area, where she remained in the bathtub unharmed. Total economic losses reached $900,000.
column49: Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted, and numerous power lines were downed by this large wedge tornado. Two mobile homes were rolled and completely destroyed, several outbuildings were destroyed, and several houses sustained damage to their roofs and walls. In Webster Parish, a building in an ATV park had part of its roof removed. One person was knocked unconscious by a flying piece of lumber. Total economic losses reached $825,000.
column50: Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted; a tree fell on a carport and a portion of a mobile home. Total economic losses reached $10,000.
column51: Numerous power lines were downed, and numerous trees were snapped or uprooted. Five homes sustained significant damage, including one that had its roof ripped off and three exterior walls collapsed. Several outbuildings were severely damaged. One person suffered an arm injury. Total economic losses reached $500,000.
column52: Numerous power lines were downed, and numerous trees were snapped or uprooted; fallen trees severely damaged one home and impacted a cemetery. A single-wide mobile home was flipped and rolled about {{convert|25|yards|m|}}, injuring a woman inside. Several barns or outbuildings were damaged, a {{convert|3000|lb|kg|abbr=on}} trailer was flipped, killing a cow, and a large television antenna was toppled onto a home.
column53: Several pine trees were snapped or uprooted, one of which fell onto a home, damaging a small antenna tower.
column54: A single-wide mobile home had a portion of its roof peeled back and a portion of one wall detached. A few small trees were snapped.
column55: Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted, one of which caused severe damage to a home. Shingles were removed from several structures.
column56: Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted in town, one of which fell on a church. A wooden barn was damaged, a gas station canopy was blown {{convert|50|yd|m|abbr=on}}, and a local business' brick facade collapsed. Storage buildings were heavily damaged as well.
column57: Picture evidence of a brief tornado was relayed.
column58: A metal shed sustained considerable damage, an outbuilding had its metal roof ripped off, and a few small trees were snapped.
column59: Mt. Olive Missionary Baptist Church and a few houses sustained roof damage. A television antenna was bent, numerous trees were snapped or uprooted, and power poles were toppled. A shed building roof collapsed, tin was blown around, and a large metal and PVC tank were blown over.
column60: Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted, many of which caused structural damage upon falling. A church sustained minor roof damage. Many mobile homes were thrown or rolled, destroying four and injuring an occupant in the process. The undercarriage of one mobile home was found wrapped around a tree.
